newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says tax shortfall could pass 8 bln DM.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says tax shortfall could pass 8 bln DM.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday the government expected a 1997 tax revenue forecast in May would fall eight billion marks ($4.6 billion) short of estimates made last November.

Speaking after negotiations with opposition Social Democrats on tax reforms, Waigel rejected SPD warnings that the May tax estimate could fall as much as 20 billion marks short of earlier expectations.
Waigel told reporters that the government's annual economic report published in January had already factored in a shortfall of eight billion marks.
Although he could not rule out a "limited increase", he said the SPD's 20 billion mark warning had was "not proved by anything".
Government budget projections have been put under pressure by an unexpected early-year surge in unemployment to the highest levels since the great depression of the 1930s.

Although Waigel has pledged to cut borrowing to qualify for European monetary union, most economists -- and even Brussels itself -- expect Germany's budget deficit to exceed the target of three percent of GDP set by the Maastricht treaty.
